recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-25736; any broader policy question about suppressing datatype invariants on pattern values should be handled separately by FHIR-I if that follow-up exists or is re-raised.
issue_request: FHIR-25736 was a Published/Persuasive MnM technical correction asking that Range constraint rng-2 ignore absent low.value or high.value when Range is used as a pattern that constrains coding metadata but not numeric values.
initial_application: Commit c4807a5165ee632872ef9f6289fee8e9e1abbb5f explicitly listed FHIR-25736 and changed source/datatypes/range.xml from low.empty()/high.empty() guards to low.value.empty()/high.value.empty() guards for R5.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Range under active [types], making source/datatypes/range.xml current build-scope source. Later commit 8a6a54029fdef0c2811fe4ea4e0286f84c1de7e3 refined the comparison to lowBoundary()/highBoundary() with a comparable() guard while retaining the FHIR-25736 value-empty semantics. Confluence minutes and Zulip discussions match the Jira resolution, and bounded searches found no conflicting later final issue.
reconciliation: No source edit was made because source/datatypes/range.xml already contains low.value.empty() or high.value.empty() before comparing low/high boundaries, so Range patterns without numeric values no longer fail rng-2 for the reason reported by the issue.
